$comment: Every stack and module the harness can install. A project chooses one or more `stacks`; each has a `language` (stacks of one language share tools), `srcDirs` (its source folders, the default answer), `detect`, a default `linter`, and the stacks it `excludes`. A module applies to the stacks or languages in its `stacks` (every stack when absent). Its files are in modules/<category>/<module>/: all/ for every stack it applies to, then <language>/, then <stack>/, a later folder replacing the same path; each is written at the same path in the project and merged with the project's edits. A module also brings: `scripts` (package.json), `checks` and `fileChecks` (what the hooks run, read from .claude/harness.json), `settings` (merged into .claude/settings.json), `mcpServers` (merged into .mcp.json), `install` (commands, each run when one of the paths it `creates` is missing; with none, every time), `mcp` (the .mcp.json servers its install adds), npm `devDependencies`, and `audit` (the rule files and skill folders, at their paths in the project, that the audit skill checks existing code against). `by.<language or stack>` holds any of these fields for one language or stack, merged over the module's own for each chosen stack (language first, then stack; a `detect` in it limits the module to stacks where it matches). `{srcDirs}` in a command is the folders of every chosen stack, or inside `by` those of its language or stack. `required` modules are always installed, `auto` ones exactly when their `detect` matches (package.json fields, or `files` that exist), and exactly one `linter` module per chosen stack is. The setup skill suggests modules by `detect` and `recommended`, and asks about them by `category` (also the folder its files are in). `renamed` maps a module's old name to its new one, for projects that still list the old.
